1008	            B_t* = E[G_t × W_t] / E[W_t]
1009	        where W_t = Σ_{j=1}^t ||s_j||² (cumulative path-variance proxy)
1010	        and ||s_j||² = 1 - 2π_j + Σπ²
1011	
1012	    The cumulative sum W_t captures the "realized energy" of trajectory has been up to timestep t,
1013	    giving higher weight to predicting rewards on high-variance paths.
1014	
1015	    Args:
1016	        token_level_rewards: Rewards at each token position [shape: (bs, response_length)]
1017	        response_mask: Binary mask for valid tokens (1) vs padding (0) [shape: (bs, response_length)]
1018	        index: Prompt indices for grouping trajectories from same prompt [shape: (bs,)]
1019	        old_log_probs: Log probabilities from training policy during generation [shape: (bs, response_length)]
1020	        sum_pi_squared: Sum of squared probabilities over vocabulary Σπ² [shape: (bs, response_length)]
1021	        rollout_is_weights: Pre-computed IS weights for W correction [shape: (bs, response_length)],
1022	            None if not using IS
1023	        handle_zero_tail: If True, zero baselines will be set in the portion of the longest trajectory
1024	            that extends beyond the second-longest trajectory in the prompt group.
1025	            Default: False
1026	        epsilon: Small constant for numerical stability (default: 1e-8)
1027	
1028	    Returns:
1029	        advantages: OTB advantage estimates [shape: (bs, response_length)]
1030	        returns: Cumulative rewards (returns) from each position [shape: (bs, response_length)]
1031	
1032	    Note on Rollout Importance Sampling:
1033	        When rollout_is_weights is provided, W_t is scaled by ρ̄²(t) to minimize MSE under truncated IS:
1034	            B_t* = Σ[G_t × ρ̄²(t) × W_t] / Σ[ρ̄²(t) × W_t]
1035	    """
1036	    with torch.no_grad():
1037	        # Compute returns (reward-to-go) for each timestep
1038	        token_returns = (token_level_rewards * response_mask).flip(dims=[-1]).cumsum(dim=-1).flip(dims=[-1])
1039	
1040	        # Step 1: Compute w_per_timestep = 1 - 2π_t + Σπ²)
1041	        pi_t = torch.exp(old_log_probs)
1042	        w_per_timestep = 1 - 2 * pi_t + sum_pi_squared
1043	
1044	        # Step 2: Apply rollout importance sampling correction (if enabled)
1045	        if rollout_is_weights is not None:
1046	            # Scale W by ρ̄² to minimize MSE under truncated IS
1047	            w_per_timestep = w_per_timestep * (rollout_is_weights**2)
1048	
1049	        # Step 3: Compute cumulative path-variance proxy: W_t = Σ_{j=1}^t w_j
1050	        # This measures accumulated variance from the start of the trajectory up to timestep t
1051	        w_cumulative = (w_per_timestep * response_mask).cumsum(dim=-1)
1052	
1053	        # Step 4: Concatenate returns and w_cumulative for each trajectory
1054	        # This allows us to compute baseline per timestep for each trajectory

1056	        max_response_length = int(response_lengths.max().item()) if response_lengths.numel() > 0 else 0

1058	            (len(response_lengths), max_response_length)

1068	
1069	        # Group trajectories by prompt
1070	        prompt_groups = defaultdict(list)
1071	        for i in range(len(response_lengths)):
1072	            if response_lengths[i] == 0:
1073	                continue
1074	            prompt_groups[index[i]].append(i)
1075	
1076	        # Compute optimal baseline for each prompt group
1077	        baselines = torch.zeros_like(all_returns)
1078	
1079	        for _, trajectory_indices in prompt_groups.items():
1080	            N = len(trajectory_indices)
1081	            traj_idx = torch.tensor(trajectory_indices, device=all_returns.device)
1082	
1083	            if N == 1:
1084	                # Single trajectory - no baseline (keep original reward as advantage)
1085	                baselines[traj_idx[0]] = 0.0
1086	                continue
1087	
1088	            # Extract group data
1089	            w_group = all_w_values[traj_idx]  # [shape: (N, max_response_length)]
1090	            R_group = all_returns[traj_idx]  # [shape: (N, max_response_length)]
1091	            # Direct optimal baseline - single value for all in group
1092	            b_star = (R_group * w_group).sum(dim=0) / (w_group.sum(dim=0) + epsilon)
1093	            # Convert to match baselines dtype (epsilon can cause float64 promotion)
1094	            baselines[traj_idx] = b_star.to(baselines.dtype)
1095	
1096	            if handle_zero_tail:
1097	                # Optionally zero out the portion of the longest trajectory that extends
1098	                # beyond the second-longest trajectory in the prompt group.
1099	                response_lengths_group = response_lengths[traj_idx]
1100	                sorted_lengths, _ = torch.sort(response_lengths_group)
1101	                max_length = int(sorted_lengths[-1].item())
1102	                second_max_length = int(sorted_lengths[-2].item())
1103	                max_length_idx = (response_lengths_group == max_length).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
1104	                if max_length_idx.numel() == 1 and max_length > second_max_length:
1105	                    max_length_traj_idx = trajectory_indices[int(max_length_idx[0])]
1106	                    baselines[max_length_traj_idx, second_max_length:] = 0.0
1107	
1108	        # Compute advantages
1109	        all_advantages = all_returns - baselines  # [shape: (bs * n, max_response_length)]
1110	
1111	        advantages = torch.zeros_like(token_returns)  # [shape: (bs * n, turn * response_length)]
1112	        for i in range(len(response_lengths)):
1113	            if response_lengths[i] == 0:
1114	                continue
1115	            advantages[i, response_mask[i].bool()] = all_advantages[i, : response_lengths[i]]
1116	
1117	        advantages = advantages * response_mask  # [shape: (bs * n * turn, response_length)]
1118	
1119	    return advantages, token_returns

1138	def agg_loss(
1139	    loss_mat: torch.Tensor,
1140	    loss_mask: torch.Tensor,
1141	    loss_agg_mode: str,
1142	    dp_size: int = 1,
1143	    batch_num_tokens: Optional[int] = None,
1144	    global_batch_size: Optional[int] = None,
1145	    loss_scale_factor: Optional[int] = None,
1146	):
1147	    """
1148	    Aggregate the loss across global batch to ensure the loss is invariant to fsdp/megatron parallelism.
1149	
1150	    NOTE: The returned loss has different behaviors for different backend:
1151	    - FSDP: the loss is directly used for backward.
1152	    - Megatron: the loss should be scaled by `num_microbatches` and `cp_size` for pp schedule.
1153	
1154	    Args:
1155	        loss_mat: micro batch loss matrix, (bs, response_length)
1156	        loss_mask: micro batch loss mask, (bs, response_length)
1157	        loss_agg_mode: method to aggregate the loss matrix into a scalar
1158	        dp_size: data parallel size
1159	        batch_num_tokens: number of valid tokens in global batch
1160	        global_batch_size: global batch size
1161	        loss_scale_factor: scale factor for "seq-mean-token-sum-norm" mode. If None, uses loss_mask.shape[-1].
1162	            Set this to a constant value to ensure consistent normalization throughout training.
1163	
1164	    Returns:
1165	        loss: `a scalar torch.Tensor`
1166	            aggregated loss
1167	    """
1168	    if loss_agg_mode == "token-mean":
1169	        if batch_num_tokens is None:
1170	            if dp_size > 1:
1171	                raise ValueError("(global) batch_num_tokens is required when dp_size > 1")
1172	            batch_num_tokens = loss_mask.sum()
1173	        loss = verl_F.masked_sum(loss_mat, loss_mask) / batch_num_tokens * dp_size
1174	    elif loss_agg_mode in ["seq-mean-token-sum", "seq-mean-token-sum-norm"]:
1175	        seq_losses = torch.sum(loss_mat * loss_mask, dim=-1)  # token-sum
1176	        seq_mask = (torch.sum(loss_mask, dim=-1) > 0).float()  # exclude fully masked sequences
1177	        if global_batch_size is None:
1178	            if dp_size > 1:
1179	                raise ValueError("global_batch_size is required when dp_size > 1")
1180	            global_batch_size = seq_mask.sum()
1181	        loss = verl_F.masked_sum(seq_losses, seq_mask) / global_batch_size * dp_size  # seq-mean
1182	        if loss_agg_mode == "seq-mean-token-sum-norm":
1183	            if loss_scale_factor is None:
1184	                horizon = loss_mask.shape[-1]
1185	                loss_scale_factor = horizon
1186	            loss /= loss_scale_factor
1187	    elif loss_agg_mode == "seq-mean-token-mean":
1188	        seq_mask = torch.sum(loss_mask, dim=-1)  # per-sequence token count
1189	        seq_losses = torch.sum(loss_mat * loss_mask, dim=-1) / (seq_mask + 1e-8)  # token-mean
1190	        seq_mask = (seq_mask > 0).float()  # exclude fully masked sequences
1191	        if global_batch_size is None:
1192	            if dp_size > 1:
1193	                raise ValueError("global_batch_size is required when dp_size > 1")
1194	            global_batch_size = seq_mask.sum()
1195	        loss = verl_F.masked_sum(seq_losses, seq_mask) / global_batch_size * dp_size  # seq-mean
1196	    else:
1197	        raise ValueError(f"Invalid loss_agg_mode: {loss_agg_mode}")
1198	
1199	    return loss

1203	def compute_policy_loss(
1204	    old_log_prob,
1205	    log_prob,
1206	    advantages,
1207	    response_mask,
1208	    cliprange=None,
1209	    cliprange_low=None,
1210	    cliprange_high=None,
1211	    clip_ratio_c=3.0,
1212	    loss_agg_mode: str = "token-mean",
1213	):
1214	    """
1215	    Compute the clipped policy objective and related metrics for PPO.
1216	
1217	    Adapted from
1218	    https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/main/trl/trainer/ppo_trainer.py#L1122
1219	
1220	    Args:
1221	        old_log_prob (torch.Tensor):
1222	            Log-probabilities of actions under the old policy, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1223	        log_prob (torch.Tensor):
1224	            Log-probabilities of actions under the current policy, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1225	        advantages (torch.Tensor):
1226	            Advantage estimates for each action, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1227	        response_mask (torch.Tensor):
1228	            Mask indicating which tokens to include in the loss, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1229	        cliprange (float, optional):
1230	            Clipping parameter ε for standard PPO. See https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.06347.
1231	            Defaults to None (must be provided).
1232	        cliprange_low (float, optional):
1233	            Lower clip range for dual-clip PPO. Defaults to same as `cliprange`.
1234	        cliprange_high (float, optional):
1235	            Upper clip range for dual-clip PPO. Defaults to same as `cliprange`.
1236	        clip_ratio_c (float, optional):
1237	            Lower bound of the ratio for dual-clip PPO. See https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.09729.
1238	            Defaults to 3.0.
1239	        loss_agg_mode (str, optional):
1240	            Aggregation mode for `agg_loss`. Defaults to "token-mean".
1241	    """
1242	    assert clip_ratio_c > 1.0, (
1243	        "The lower bound of the clip_ratio_c for dual-clip PPO should be greater than 1.0,"
1244	        + f" but get the value: {clip_ratio_c}."
1245	    )
1246	
1247	    negative_approx_kl = log_prob - old_log_prob
1248	    # Clamp negative_approx_kl for stability
1249	    negative_approx_kl = torch.clamp(negative_approx_kl, min=-20.0, max=20.0)
1250	    ratio = torch.exp(negative_approx_kl)
1251	    ppo_kl = verl_F.masked_mean(-negative_approx_kl, response_mask)
1252	
1253	    pg_losses1 = -advantages * ratio
1254	    if cliprange_low is None:
1255	        cliprange_low = cliprange
1256	    if cliprange_high is None:
1257	        cliprange_high = cliprange
1258	    pg_losses2 = -advantages * torch.clamp(
1259	        ratio, 1 - cliprange_low, 1 + cliprange_high
1260	    )  # - clip(ratio, 1-cliprange, 1+cliprange) * A
1261	    clip_pg_losses1 = torch.maximum(
1262	        pg_losses1, pg_losses2
1263	    )  # max(-ratio * A, -clip(ratio, 1-cliprange, 1+cliprange) * A)
1264	    pg_clipfrac = verl_F.masked_mean(torch.gt(pg_losses2, pg_losses1).float(), response_mask)
1265	
1266	    pg_losses3 = -advantages * clip_ratio_c
1267	    clip_pg_losses2 = torch.min(pg_losses3, clip_pg_losses1)
1268	    pg_clipfrac_lower = verl_F.masked_mean(
1269	        torch.gt(clip_pg_losses1, pg_losses3) * (advantages < 0).float(), response_mask
1270	    )
1271	
1272	    pg_losses = torch.where(advantages < 0, clip_pg_losses2, clip_pg_losses1)
1273	    pg_loss = agg_loss(loss_mat=pg_losses, loss_mask=response_mask, loss_agg_mode=loss_agg_mode)
1274	
1275	    return pg_loss, pg_clipfrac, ppo_kl, pg_clipfrac_lower

1373	def compute_policy_loss_dppo_tv(
1374	    old_log_prob: torch.Tensor,
1375	    log_prob: torch.Tensor,
1376	    advantages: torch.Tensor,
1377	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
1378	    loss_agg_mode: str = "token-mean",
1379	    config: Optional[ActorConfig] = None,
1380	    rollout_is_weights: torch.Tensor | None = None,
1381	) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[str, Any]]:
1382	    """
1383	    Compute the clipped policy objective and related metrics for DPPO-Binary-TV.
1384	
1385	    See https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.04879 for more details.
1386	
1387	    Args:
1388	        old_log_prob (torch.Tensor):
1389	            Log-probabilities of actions under the old policy, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1390	        log_prob (torch.Tensor):
1391	            Log-probabilities of actions under the current policy, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1392	        advantages (torch.Tensor):
1393	            Advantage estimates for each action, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1394	        response_mask (torch.Tensor):
1395	            Mask indicating which tokens to include in the loss, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1396	        loss_agg_mode (str, optional):
1397	            Aggregation mode for `agg_loss`. Defaults to "token-mean".
1398	        config: `(verl.trainer.config.ActorConfig)`:
1399	            config for the actor.
1400	        rollout_log_probs: `(torch.Tensor)`:
1401	            log probabilities of actions under the rollout policy, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1402	    """
1403	
1404	    assert config is not None
1405	    assert not isinstance(config, AlgoConfig)
1406	    # Note: the clip_ratio is different from the standard PPO, it is the TV divergence threshold for DPPO.
1407	    clip_divergence = config.clip_ratio
1408	    clip_divergence_low = config.clip_ratio_low if config.clip_ratio_low is not None else clip_divergence
1409	    clip_divergence_high = config.clip_ratio_high if config.clip_ratio_high is not None else clip_divergence
1410	
1411	    negative_approx_kl = log_prob - old_log_prob
1412	    # Clamp negative_approx_kl for stability
1413	    negative_approx_kl = torch.clamp(negative_approx_kl, min=-20.0, max=20.0)
1414	    ratio = torch.exp(negative_approx_kl)
1415	    ppo_kl = verl_F.masked_mean(-negative_approx_kl, response_mask)
1416	
1417	    # Instead of dual-clip PPO, we use truncated importance sampling (TIS) to clip the policy loss.
1418	    # However, a large threshold is recommended to avoid performance degradation due to the truncation bias.
1419	    # See Section 5.4 in https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.04879 for more details.
1420	    clip_ratio_c = config.get("clip_ratio_c", 20.0)
1421	    truncated_ratio = torch.clamp(ratio, max=clip_ratio_c)
1422	    truncated_ratio = truncated_ratio.detach()
1423	
1424	    # Compute valid mask for DPPO-Binary-TV
1425	    prob = torch.exp(log_prob)
1426	    old_prob = torch.exp(old_log_prob)
1427	    valid_positive_mask = (prob - old_prob) <= clip_divergence_high
1428	    valid_negative_mask = (prob - old_prob) >= -clip_divergence_low
1429	    valid_mask = torch.where(advantages > 0, valid_positive_mask, valid_negative_mask)
1430	    valid_mask = valid_mask.detach().float()
1431	
1432	    pg_losses = -advantages * truncated_ratio * log_prob * valid_mask
1433	
1434	    # Apply rollout correction weights if provided
1435	    if rollout_is_weights is not None:
1436	        pg_losses = pg_losses * rollout_is_weights
1437	
1438	    pg_loss = agg_loss(
1439	        loss_mat=pg_losses, loss_mask=response_mask, loss_agg_mode=loss_agg_mode, **config.global_batch_info
1440	    )
1441	
1442	    pg_clipfrac = verl_F.masked_mean((1.0 - valid_mask).float(), response_mask)
1443	    pg_clipfrac_lower = verl_F.masked_mean((ratio > clip_ratio_c).float() * valid_mask, response_mask)
1444	
1445	    pg_metrics = {
1446	        "actor/pg_clipfrac": pg_clipfrac.detach().item(),
1447	        "actor/ppo_kl": ppo_kl.detach().item(),
1448	        "actor/pg_clipfrac_lower": pg_clipfrac_lower.detach().item(),
1449	    }
1450	    return pg_loss, pg_metrics

1455	    old_log_prob: torch.Tensor,
1456	    log_prob: torch.Tensor,
1457	    advantages: torch.Tensor,
1458	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
1459	    loss_agg_mode: str = "token-mean",
1460	    config: Optional[ActorConfig] = None,
1461	    rollout_is_weights: torch.Tensor | None = None,
1462	) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[str, Any]]:
1463	    """
1464	    Compute the clipped policy objective and related metrics for DPPO-Binary-KL.
1465	
1466	    See https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.04879 for more details.
1467	
1468	    Args:
1469	        old_log_prob (torch.Tensor):
1470	            Log-probabilities of actions under the old policy, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1471	        log_prob (torch.Tensor):
1472	            Log-probabilities of actions under the current policy, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1473	        advantages (torch.Tensor):
1474	            Advantage estimates for each action, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1475	        response_mask (torch.Tensor):
1476	            Mask indicating which tokens to include in the loss, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1477	        loss_agg_mode (str, optional):
1478	            Aggregation mode for `agg_loss`. Defaults to "token-mean".
1479	        config: `(verl.trainer.config.ActorConfig)`:
1480	            config for the actor.
1481	        rollout_log_probs: `(torch.Tensor)`:
1482	            log probabilities of actions under the rollout policy, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1483	    """
1484	
1485	    assert config is not None
1486	    assert not isinstance(config, AlgoConfig)
1487	    # Note: the clip_ratio is different from the standard PPO, it is the KL divergence threshold for DPPO.
1488	    clip_divergence = config.clip_ratio
1489	    clip_divergence_low = config.clip_ratio_low if config.clip_ratio_low is not None else clip_divergence
1490	    clip_divergence_high = config.clip_ratio_high if config.clip_ratio_high is not None else clip_divergence
1491	
1492	    negative_approx_kl = log_prob - old_log_prob
1493	    # Clamp negative_approx_kl for stability
1494	    negative_approx_kl = torch.clamp(negative_approx_kl, min=-20.0, max=20.0)
1495	    ratio = torch.exp(negative_approx_kl)
1496	    ppo_kl = verl_F.masked_mean(-negative_approx_kl, response_mask)
1497	
1498	    # Instead of dual-clip PPO, we use truncated importance sampling (TIS) to clip the policy loss.
1499	    # However, a large threshold is recommended to avoid performance degradation due to the truncation bias.
1500	    # See Section 5.4 in https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.04879 for more details.
1501	    clip_ratio_c = config.get("clip_ratio_c", 20.0)
1502	    truncated_ratio = torch.clamp(ratio, max=clip_ratio_c)
1503	    truncated_ratio = truncated_ratio.detach()
1504	
1505	    # Compute valid mask for DPPO-Binary-KL
1506	    prob = torch.exp(log_prob)
1507	    old_prob = torch.exp(old_log_prob)
1508	    binary_kl = old_prob * (old_log_prob - log_prob) + (1 - old_prob) * torch.log(
1509	        (1.0 - old_prob + 1e-8) / (1.0 - prob + 1e-8)
1510	    )
1511	    valid_positive_mask = (binary_kl <= clip_divergence_high) | (prob <= old_prob)
1512	    valid_negative_mask = (binary_kl <= clip_divergence_low) | (prob >= old_prob)
1513	    valid_mask = torch.where(advantages > 0, valid_positive_mask, valid_negative_mask)
1514	    valid_mask = valid_mask.detach().float()
1515	
1516	    pg_losses = -advantages * truncated_ratio * log_prob * valid_mask
1517

1524	    )
1525

1538	@register_policy_loss("gspo")
1539	def compute_policy_loss_gspo(
1540	    old_log_prob: torch.Tensor,
1541	    log_prob: torch.Tensor,
1542	    advantages: torch.Tensor,
1543	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
1544	    loss_agg_mode: str = "seq-mean-token-mean",
1545	    config: Optional[ActorConfig] = None,
1546	    rollout_is_weights: torch.Tensor | None = None,
1547	) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[str, Any]]:
1548	    """
1549	    Compute the clipped policy objective and related metrics for GSPO.
1550	
1551	    See https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.18071 for more details.
1552	
1553	    Args:
1554	        old_log_prob (torch.Tensor):
1555	            Log-probabilities of actions under the old policy, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1556	        log_prob (torch.Tensor):
1557	            Log-probabilities of actions under the current policy, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1558	        advantages (torch.Tensor):
1559	            Advantage estimates for each action, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1560	        response_mask (torch.Tensor):
1561	            Mask indicating which tokens to include in the loss, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1562	        loss_agg_mode (str, optional):
1563	            Aggregation mode for `agg_loss`. For GSPO, it is recommended to use "seq-mean-token-mean".
1564	    """
1565	
1566	    assert config is not None
1567	    assert isinstance(config, ActorConfig)
1568	    clip_ratio_low = config.clip_ratio_low if config.clip_ratio_low is not None else config.clip_ratio
1569	    clip_ratio_high = config.clip_ratio_high if config.clip_ratio_high is not None else config.clip_ratio
1570	
1571	    negative_approx_kl = log_prob - old_log_prob
1572	
1573	    # compute sequence-level importance ratio:
1574	    # si(θ) = (π_θ(yi|x)/π_θold(yi|x))^(1/|yi|) =
1575	    # exp [(1/|y_i|) * Σ_t log(π_θ(y_i,t|x,y_i,<t)/π_θold(y_i,t|x,y_i,<t))]
1576	    seq_lengths = torch.sum(response_mask, dim=-1).clamp(min=1)
1577	    negative_approx_kl_seq = torch.sum(negative_approx_kl * response_mask, dim=-1) / seq_lengths
1578	
1579	    # Combined ratio at token level:
1580	    # s_i,t(θ) = sg[s_i(θ)] · π_θ(y_i,t|x, y_i,<t) / sg[π_θ(y_i,t|x, y_i,<t)]
1581	    # In log space: log(s_i,t(θ)) = sg[log(s_i(θ))] + log_prob - sg[log_prob]
1582	    log_seq_importance_ratio = log_prob - log_prob.detach() + negative_approx_kl_seq.detach().unsqueeze(-1)
1583	    log_seq_importance_ratio = torch.clamp(log_seq_importance_ratio, max=10.0)  # clamp for numerical stability
1584	
1585	    # finaly exp() to remove log
1586	    seq_importance_ratio = torch.exp(log_seq_importance_ratio)
1587	
1588	    pg_losses1 = -advantages * seq_importance_ratio
1589	    pg_losses2 = -advantages * torch.clamp(seq_importance_ratio, 1 - clip_ratio_low, 1 + clip_ratio_high)
1590	    pg_losses = torch.maximum(pg_losses1, pg_losses2)
1591	
1592	    # Apply rollout correction weights if provided
1593	    if rollout_is_weights is not None:
1594	        pg_losses = pg_losses * rollout_is_weights
1595	
1596	    # for GSPO, we need to aggregate the loss at the sequence level (seq-mean-token-mean)
1597	    pg_loss = agg_loss(
1598	        loss_mat=pg_losses, loss_mask=response_mask, loss_agg_mode="seq-mean-token-mean", **config.global_batch_info
1599	    )
1600	
1601	    # For compatibility, return zero for pg_clipfrac_lower (not used in standard GSPO)
1602	    pg_clipfrac = verl_F.masked_mean(torch.gt(pg_losses2, pg_losses1).float(), response_mask)
1603	    pg_clipfrac_lower = torch.tensor(0.0, device=pg_loss.device)
1604	
1605	    ppo_kl = verl_F.masked_mean(-negative_approx_kl, response_mask)
1606	    pg_metrics = {
1607	        "actor/pg_clipfrac": pg_clipfrac.detach().item(),
1608	        "actor/ppo_kl": ppo_kl.detach().item(),
1609	        "actor/pg_clipfrac_lower": pg_clipfrac_lower.detach().item(),
1610	    }
1611	    return pg_loss, pg_metrics

1614	@register_policy_loss("sapo")
1615	def compute_policy_loss_sapo(
1616	    old_log_prob: torch.Tensor,
1617	    log_prob: torch.Tensor,
1618	    advantages: torch.Tensor,
1619	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
1620	    loss_agg_mode: str = "seq-mean-token-mean",
1621	    config: Optional[ActorConfig] = None,
1622	    rollout_is_weights: torch.Tensor | None = None,
1623	) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[str, Any]]:
1624	    """
1625	    Compute the smoothed policy objective and related metrics for SAPO.
1626	
1627	    See https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.20347 for more details.
1628	
1629	    Args:
1630	        old_log_prob (torch.Tensor):
1631	            Log-probabilities of actions under the old policy, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1632	        log_prob (torch.Tensor):
1633	            Log-probabilities of actions under the current policy, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1634	        advantages (torch.Tensor):
1635	            Advantage estimates for each action, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1636	        response_mask (torch.Tensor):
1637	            Mask indicating which tokens to include in the loss, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1638	        loss_agg_mode (str, optional):
1639	            Aggregation mode for `agg_loss`. For SAPO, it is recommended to use "seq-mean-token-mean".
1640	    """
1641	
1642	    assert config is not None
1643	    assert isinstance(config, ActorConfig)
1644	
1645	    # temperature for positive and negative token updates
1646	    tau_pos = torch.as_tensor(config.tau_pos, dtype=advantages.dtype, device=advantages.device)
1647	    tau_neg = torch.as_tensor(config.tau_neg, dtype=advantages.dtype, device=advantages.device)
1648	
1649	    def gate_function(x, tau):
1650	        """The gating function used in SAPO"""
1651	        return torch.sigmoid(tau * (x - 1.0)) * (4.0 / tau)
1652	
1653	    # compute IS at token level:
1654	    # r_{i,t}(θ) = π_θ(y_{i,t}|x, y_{i,<t}) / π_θold(y_{i,t}|x, y_{i,<t})]
1655	    # In log space: log(r_{i,t}(θ)) = log_prob - ol_log_prob
1656	    negative_approx_kl = log_prob - old_log_prob
1657	    # Clamp negative_approx_kl for stability
1658	    negative_approx_kl = torch.clamp(negative_approx_kl, min=-20.0, max=20.0)
1659	    # finally exp() to remove log and get r_{i,t}(θ)
1660	    ratio = torch.exp(negative_approx_kl)
1661	
1662	    # tau_{i,t} is tau_pos if adv > 0 else tau_neg
1663	    taus = torch.where(
1664	        condition=advantages > 0,
1665	        input=tau_pos,  # if A_{i,t} > 0 we set to tau_pos
1666	        other=tau_neg,  # if A_{i,t} <= 0 we set to tau_neg
1667	    )
1668	
1669	    # compute the gates f_{i,t}(r_{i,t}(θ)) at token level
1670	    gates = gate_function(ratio, taus)
1671	
1672	    # compute policy gradient loss
1673	    pg_losses = -gates * advantages
1674	
1675	    # Apply rollout correction weights if provided
1676	    if rollout_is_weights is not None:
1677	        pg_losses = pg_losses * rollout_is_weights
1678	
1679	    # for SAPO, we need to aggregate the loss at the sequence level (seq-mean-token-mean)
1680	    pg_loss = agg_loss(
1681	        loss_mat=pg_losses, loss_mask=response_mask, loss_agg_mode="seq-mean-token-mean", **config.global_batch_info
1682	    )
1683	
1684	    # For compatibility, return zero for both pg_clipfrac and pg_clipfrac_lower (not used in SAPO)
1685	    pg_clipfrac = torch.tensor(0.0, device=pg_loss.device)
1686	    pg_clipfrac_lower = torch.tensor(0.0, device=pg_loss.device)
1687	    # compute KL for metrics tracking
1688	    ppo_kl = verl_F.masked_mean(-negative_approx_kl, response_mask)
1689	    # return metrics dict
1690	    pg_metrics = {
1691	        "actor/pg_clipfrac": pg_clipfrac.detach().item(),
1692	        "actor/ppo_kl": ppo_kl.detach().item(),
1693	        "actor/pg_clipfrac_lower": pg_clipfrac_lower.detach().item(),
1694	    }
1695	
1696	    return pg_loss, pg_metrics

1735	@register_policy_loss("clip_cov")
1736	def compute_policy_loss_clip_cov(
1737	    old_log_prob: torch.Tensor,
1738	    log_prob: torch.Tensor,
1739	    advantages: torch.Tensor,
1740	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
1741	    loss_agg_mode: str = "token-mean",
1742	    config: Optional[ActorConfig] = None,
1743	    rollout_is_weights: torch.Tensor | None = None,
1744	) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[str, Any]]:
1745	    """
1746	    Compute the clipped policy objective and related metrics for Clip-Cov.
1747	
1748	    Adapted from
1749	    https://github.com/PRIME-RL/Entropy-Mechanism-of-RL/blob/main/verl/trainer/ppo/core_algos.py
1750	
1751	    Args:
1752	        old_log_prob (torch.Tensor):
1753	            Log-probabilities of actions under the old policy, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1754	        log_prob (torch.Tensor):
1755	            Log-probabilities of actions under the current policy, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1756	        advantages (torch.Tensor):
1757	            Advantage estimates for each action, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1758	        response_mask (torch.Tensor):
1759	            Mask indicating which tokens to include in the loss, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1760	        cliprange (float, optional):
1761	            Clipping parameter ε for standard PPO. See https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.06347.
1762	            Defaults to None (must be provided).
1763	        cliprange_low (float, optional):
1764	            Lower clip range for dual-clip PPO. Defaults to same as `cliprange`.
1765	        cliprange_high (float, optional):
1766	            Upper clip range for dual-clip PPO. Defaults to same as `cliprange`.
1767	        loss_agg_mode (str, optional):
1768	            Aggregation mode for `agg_loss`. Defaults to "token-mean".
1769	        clip_cov_ratio (float, optional):
1770	            Ratio for clipping the covariance. Defaults to 0.0002.
1771	        clip_cov_lb (float, optional):
1772	            Lower bound for clipping covariance. Defaults to 1.0.
1773	        clip_cov_ub (float, optional):
1774	            Upper bound for clipping covariance. Defaults to 5.0.
1775	    """
1776	    assert config is not None
1777	    assert not isinstance(config, AlgoConfig), "passing AlgoConfig not supported yet"
1778	    assert config.policy_loss is not None
1779	
1780	    clip_cov_ratio = config.policy_loss.clip_cov_ratio if config.policy_loss.clip_cov_ratio is not None else 0.0002
1781	    cliprange = config.clip_ratio
1782	    cliprange_low = config.clip_ratio_low if config.clip_ratio_low is not None else cliprange
1783	    cliprange_high = config.clip_ratio_high if config.clip_ratio_high is not None else cliprange
1784	    clip_cov_ub = config.policy_loss.clip_cov_ub if config.policy_loss.clip_cov_ub is not None else 5.0
1785	    clip_cov_lb = config.policy_loss.clip_cov_lb if config.policy_loss.clip_cov_lb is not None else 1.0
1786	
1787	    assert clip_cov_ratio > 0, "clip_ratio should be larger than 0."
1788	
1789	    negative_approx_kl = log_prob - old_log_prob
1790	    ratio = torch.exp(negative_approx_kl)
1791	    ppo_kl = verl_F.masked_mean(-negative_approx_kl, response_mask)
1792	
1793	    pg_losses1 = -advantages * ratio
1794	
1795	    if cliprange_low is None:
1796	        cliprange_low = cliprange
1797	    if cliprange_high is None:
1798	        cliprange_high = cliprange
1799	
1800	    corr = torch.ones_like(advantages)
1801	    pg_losses2 = -advantages * torch.clamp(ratio, 1 - cliprange_low, 1 + cliprange_high)
1802	    clip_by_origin = (pg_losses2 > pg_losses1) & (response_mask > 0)
1803	
1804	    cov_all = (advantages - verl_F.masked_mean(advantages, response_mask)) * (
1805	        log_prob - verl_F.masked_mean(log_prob.detach(), response_mask)
1806	    )
1807	    cov_all[response_mask == 0] = -torch.inf
1808	    cov_all[clip_by_origin] = -torch.inf
1809	
1810	    clip_num = max(int(clip_cov_ratio * response_mask.sum().item()), 1)
1811	    top_k_idx = (cov_all < clip_cov_ub) & (cov_all > clip_cov_lb) & (response_mask > 0)
1812	    top_k_idx = torch.nonzero(top_k_idx)
1813	
1814	    if len(top_k_idx) > 0:
1815	        perm = torch.randperm(len(top_k_idx))
1816	        top_k_idx = top_k_idx[perm[: min(clip_num, len(top_k_idx))]]
1817	    else:
1818	        top_k_idx = torch.empty((0, 2), device=cov_all.device, dtype=torch.long)
1819	
1820	    corr[top_k_idx[:, 0], top_k_idx[:, 1]] = 0
1821	
1822	    pg_clipfrac = verl_F.masked_mean((corr == 0).float(), response_mask)
1823	
1824	    pg_losses = torch.maximum(pg_losses1, pg_losses2) * corr
1825	
1826	    # Apply rollout correction weights if provided
1827	    if rollout_is_weights is not None:
1828	        pg_losses = pg_losses * rollout_is_weights
1829	
1830	    pg_loss = agg_loss(
1831	        loss_mat=pg_losses, loss_mask=response_mask, loss_agg_mode=loss_agg_mode, **config.global_batch_info
1832	    )
1833	    pg_metrics = {
1834	        "actor/pg_clipfrac": pg_clipfrac.detach().item(),
1835	        "actor/ppo_kl": ppo_kl.detach().item(),
1836	    }
1837	    return pg_loss, pg_metrics

1840	@register_policy_loss("kl_cov")
1841	def compute_policy_loss_kl_cov(
1842	    old_log_prob: torch.Tensor,
1843	    log_prob: torch.Tensor,
1844	    advantages: torch.Tensor,
1845	    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
1846	    loss_agg_mode: str = "token-mean",
1847	    config: Optional[ActorConfig] = None,
1848	    rollout_is_weights: torch.Tensor | None = None,
1849	) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[str, Any]]:
1850	    """
1851	    Compute the clipped policy objective and related metrics for Clip-Cov.
1852	
1853	    Adapted from
1854	    https://github.com/PRIME-RL/Entropy-Mechanism-of-RL/blob/main/verl/trainer/ppo/core_algos.py
1855	
1856	    Args:
1857	        old_log_prob (torch.Tensor):
1858	            Log-probabilities of actions under the old policy, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1859	        log_prob (torch.Tensor):
1860	            Log-probabilities of actions under the current policy, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1861	        advantages (torch.Tensor):
1862	            Advantage estimates for each action, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1863	        response_mask (torch.Tensor):
1864	            Mask indicating which tokens to include in the loss, shape (batch_size, response_length).
1865	        loss_agg_mode (str, optional):
1866	            Aggregation mode for `agg_loss`. Defaults to "token-mean".
1867	        kl_cov_ratio (float, optional):
1868	            Ratio for selecting the top-k covariance values. Defaults to 0.0002.
1869	        ppo_kl_coef (float, optional):
1870	            Coefficient for the KL penalty term in the loss. Defaults to 1.
1871	    """
1872	    assert config is not None
1873	    assert not isinstance(config, AlgoConfig), "passing AlgoConfig not supported yet"
1874	    assert config.policy_loss is not None
1875	
1876	    kl_cov_ratio = config.policy_loss.kl_cov_ratio if config.policy_loss.kl_cov_ratio is not None else 0.0002
1877	    ppo_kl_coef = config.policy_loss.ppo_kl_coef if config.policy_loss.ppo_kl_coef is not None else 1.0
1878	
1879	    assert kl_cov_ratio > 0, "kl_cov_ratio should be larger than 0."
1880	
1881	    negative_approx_kl = log_prob - old_log_prob
1882	    abs_kl = negative_approx_kl.abs()
1883	    ratio = torch.exp(negative_approx_kl)
1884	    ppo_kl_abs = verl_F.masked_mean(negative_approx_kl.abs(), response_mask)
1885	    pg_losses1 = -advantages * ratio
1886	    pg_losses_kl = -advantages * ratio + ppo_kl_coef * abs_kl
1887	    pg_losses = pg_losses1
1888	
1889	    all_valid = response_mask > 0
1890	    all_valid_idx = torch.nonzero(all_valid.reshape(-1), as_tuple=True)[0]
1891	    all_valid_adv = advantages[all_valid].detach().reshape(-1).cpu()
1892	    all_valid_logp = log_prob[all_valid].detach().reshape(-1).cpu()
1893	
1894	    k = min(kl_cov_ratio, len(all_valid_adv))
1895	
1896	    if k != 0:
1897	        cov_lst_all = (all_valid_adv - all_valid_adv.mean()) * (all_valid_logp - all_valid_logp.mean())
1898	        k_percent_nums = max(1, int(len(cov_lst_all) * kl_cov_ratio))
1899	        large_cov_idxs = torch.topk(cov_lst_all, k_percent_nums, largest=True).indices
1900	
1901	        if len(large_cov_idxs) != 0:
1902	            large_cov_idxs = all_valid_idx[large_cov_idxs]
1903	            pg_losses[large_cov_idxs // advantages.shape[1], large_cov_idxs % advantages.shape[1]] = pg_losses_kl[
1904	                large_cov_idxs // advantages.shape[1], large_cov_idxs % advantages.shape[1]
1905	            ]
1906	
1907	    # Apply rollout correction weights if provided
1908	    if rollout_is_weights is not None:
1909	        pg_losses = pg_losses * rollout_is_weights
1910	
1911	    pg_loss = agg_loss(
1912	        loss_mat=pg_losses, loss_mask=response_mask, loss_agg_mode=loss_agg_mode, **config.global_batch_info
1913	    )
1914	    pg_metrics = {
1915	        "actor/ppo_kl": ppo_kl_abs.detach().item(),
1916	    }
1917	    return pg_loss, pg_metrics
1918

1954	
1955	    cliprange = clip_ratio
1956	    cliprange_low = clip_ratio_low
1957	    cliprange_high = clip_ratio_high

"""
Core functions to implement PPO algorithms.
The function implemented in this file should be used by trainer with different distributed strategies to
implement PPO-like algorithms.
"""

__all__ = ["register_adv_est", "get_adv_estimator_fn", "AdvantageEstimator"]

from collections import defaultdict
from enum import Enum
from typing import Any, Callable, Optional

import numpy as np
import torch
from omegaconf import DictConfig

from verl.utils import as_torch_index, group_mean_std
from verl.utils.import_utils import deprecated
from verl.workers.config import ActorConfig

PolicyLossFn = Callable[
    [
        torch.Tensor,  # old_log_prob
        torch.Tensor,  # log_prob
        torch.Tensor,  # advantages
        torch.Tensor,  # response_mask
        str,  # loss_agg_mode
        Optional[DictConfig | ActorConfig],  # config
        torch.Tensor | None,  # rollout_log_probs
    ],
    tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[str, Any]],
]

POLICY_LOSS_REGISTRY: dict[str, PolicyLossFn] = {}


def register_policy_loss(name: str) -> Callable[[PolicyLossFn], PolicyLossFn]:
    """Register a policy loss function with the given name.

    Args:
        name (str): The name to register the policy loss function under.

    Returns:
        function: Decorator function that registers the policy loss function.
    """

    def decorator(func: PolicyLossFn) -> PolicyLossFn:
        POLICY_LOSS_REGISTRY[name] = func
        return func

    return decorator


def get_policy_loss_fn(name):
    """Get the policy loss with a given name.

    Args:
        name: `(str)`
            The name of the policy loss.

    Returns:
        `(callable)`: The policy loss function.
    """
    loss_name = name
    if loss_name not in POLICY_LOSS_REGISTRY:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unsupported loss mode: {loss_name}. Supported modes are: {list(POLICY_LOSS_REGISTRY.keys())}"
        )
    return POLICY_LOSS_REGISTRY[loss_name]


class AdvantageEstimator(str, Enum):
    """Using an enumeration class to avoid spelling errors in adv_estimator.

    Note(haibin.lin): this enum class is immutable after creation. Extending this
    enum for new estimators may not be necessary since users can always just call
    `verl.trainer.ppo.core_algos.register` with string name for a custom advantage
    estimator instead.
    """

    GAE = "gae"
    GRPO = "grpo"
    REINFORCE_PLUS_PLUS = "reinforce_plus_plus"
    REINFORCE_PLUS_PLUS_BASELINE = "reinforce_plus_plus_baseline"
    REMAX = "remax"
    RLOO = "rloo"
    OPO = "opo"
    GRPO_PASSK = "grpo_passk"
    GPG = "gpg"
    RLOO_VECTORIZED = "rloo_vectorized"
    GRPO_VECTORIZED = "grpo_vectorized"
    OPTIMAL_TOKEN_BASELINE = "optimal_token_baseline"
    TIR_OPTIMAL_TOKEN_BASELINE = "tir_optimal_token_baseline"
    GDPO = "gdpo"


ADV_ESTIMATOR_REGISTRY: dict[str, Any] = {}


def register_adv_est(name_or_enum: str | AdvantageEstimator) -> Any:
    """Decorator to register a advantage estimator function with a given name.

    Args:
        name_or_enum: `(str)` or `(AdvantageEstimator)`
            The name or enum of the advantage estimator.

    """

    def decorator(fn):
        name = name_or_enum.value if isinstance(name_or_enum, Enum) else name_or_enum
        if name in ADV_ESTIMATOR_REGISTRY and ADV_ESTIMATOR_REGISTRY[name] != fn:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Adv estimator {name} has already been registered: {ADV_ESTIMATOR_REGISTRY[name]} vs {fn}"
            )
        ADV_ESTIMATOR_REGISTRY[name] = fn
        return fn

    return decorator


def get_adv_estimator_fn(name_or_enum):
    """Get the advantage estimator function with a given name.

    Args:
        name_or_enum: `(str)` or `(AdvantageEstimator)`
            The name or enum of the advantage estimator.

    Returns:
        `(callable)`: The advantage estimator function.
    """
    name = name_or_enum.value if isinstance(name_or_enum, Enum) else name_or_enum
    if name not in ADV_ESTIMATOR_REGISTRY:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown advantage estimator simply: {name}")
    return ADV_ESTIMATOR_REGISTRY[name]


class AdaptiveKLController:
    """
    Adaptive KL controller described in the paper:
    https://arxiv.org/pdf/1909.08593.pdf
    """

    def __init__(self, init_kl_coef, target_kl, horizon):
        self.value = init_kl_coef
        self.target = target_kl
        self.horizon = horizon

    def update(self, current_kl, n_steps):
        """Update the KL coefficient based on current KL divergence.

        Args:
            current_kl (float): Current KL divergence value.
            n_steps (int): Number of steps taken.
        """
        target = self.target
        proportional_error = np.clip(current_kl / target - 1, -0.2, 0.2)
        mult = 1 + proportional_error * n_steps / self.horizon
        self.value *= mult


class FixedKLController:
    """Fixed KL controller."""

    def __init__(self, kl_coef):
        self.value = kl_coef

    def update(self, current_kl, n_steps):
        """Update method for fixed KL controller (no-op).

        Args:
            current_kl (float): Current KL divergence value (unused).
            n_steps (int): Number of steps taken (unused).
        """
        pass


def get_kl_controller(kl_ctrl):
    """Factory function to create appropriate KL controller based on configuration.

    Args:
        kl_ctrl: Configuration object containing KL controller settings.

    Returns:
        KL controller instance (FixedKLController or AdaptiveKLController).

    Raises:
        NotImplementedError: If controller type is not supported.
        AssertionError: If adaptive controller horizon is not positive.
    """
    if kl_ctrl.type == "fixed":
        return FixedKLController(kl_coef=kl_ctrl.kl_coef)
    elif kl_ctrl.type == "adaptive":
        assert kl_ctrl.horizon > 0, f"horizon must be larger than 0. Got {kl_ctrl.horizon}"
        return AdaptiveKLController(init_kl_coef=kl_ctrl.kl_coef, target_kl=kl_ctrl.target_kl, horizon=kl_ctrl.horizon)
    else:
        raise NotImplementedError


@register_adv_est(AdvantageEstimator.GAE)  # or simply: @register_adv_est("gae")
def compute_gae_advantage_return(
    token_level_rewards: torch.Tensor,
    values: torch.Tensor,
    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
    gamma: torch.Tensor,
    lam: torch.Tensor,
):
    """Adapted from https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/main/trl/trainer/ppo_trainer.py

    Args:
        token_level_rewards: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape is (bs, response_length)
        values: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape is (bs, response_length)
        response_mask: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape is (bs, response_length). [EOS] mask. The token after [EOS] have mask zero.
        gamma is `(float)`
            discounted factor used in RL
        lam: `(float)`
            lambda value when computing Generalized Advantage Estimation (https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02438)

    Returns:
        advantages: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
        Returns: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)

    """
    with torch.no_grad():
        nextvalues = 0
        lastgaelam = 0
        advantages_reversed = []
        gen_len = token_level_rewards.shape[-1]

        for t in reversed(range(gen_len)):
            delta = token_level_rewards[:, t] + gamma * nextvalues - values[:, t]
            lastgaelam_ = delta + gamma * lam * lastgaelam

            # skip values and TD-error on observation tokens
            nextvalues = values[:, t] * response_mask[:, t] + (1 - response_mask[:, t]) * nextvalues
            lastgaelam = lastgaelam_ * response_mask[:, t] + (1 - response_mask[:, t]) * lastgaelam

            advantages_reversed.append(lastgaelam)
        advantages = torch.stack(advantages_reversed[::-1], dim=1)

        returns = advantages + values
        advantages = verl_F.masked_whiten(advantages, response_mask)
    return advantages, returns


# NOTE(sgm): this implementation only consider outcome supervision, where the reward is a scalar.
@register_adv_est(AdvantageEstimator.GRPO)  # or simply: @register_adv_est("grpo")
def compute_grpo_outcome_advantage(
    token_level_rewards: torch.Tensor,
    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
    index: np.ndarray,
    epsilon: float = 1e-6,
    norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo: bool = True,
    config: Optional[AlgoConfig] = None,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    Compute advantage for GRPO, operating only on Outcome reward
    (with only one scalar reward for each response).

    Args:
        token_level_rewards: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape is (bs, response_length)
        response_mask: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape is (bs, response_length)
        index: `(np.ndarray)`
            index array for grouping
        epsilon: `(float)`
            small value to avoid division by zero
        norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo: `(bool)`
            whether to scale the GRPO advantage
        config: `(Optional[AlgoConfig])`
            algorithm configuration object

    Note:
        If norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo is True, the advantage is scaled by the std, as in the original GRPO.
        If False, the advantage is not scaled, as in Dr.GRPO (https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.20783).

    Returns:
        advantages: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape is (bs, response_length)
        Returns: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape is (bs, response_length)
    """
    scores = token_level_rewards.sum(dim=-1)

    id2score = defaultdict(list)
    id2mean = {}
    id2std = {}

    with torch.no_grad():
        bsz = scores.shape[0]
        for i in range(bsz):
            id2score[index[i]].append(scores[i])
        for idx in id2score:
            if len(id2score[idx]) == 1:
                id2mean[idx] = torch.tensor(0.0)
                id2std[idx] = torch.tensor(1.0)
            elif len(id2score[idx]) > 1:
                scores_tensor = torch.stack(id2score[idx])
                id2mean[idx] = torch.mean(scores_tensor)
                id2std[idx] = torch.std(scores_tensor)
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"no score in prompt index: {idx}")
        for i in range(bsz):
            if norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo:
                scores[i] = (scores[i] - id2mean[index[i]]) / (id2std[index[i]] + epsilon)
            else:
                scores[i] = scores[i] - id2mean[index[i]]
        scores = scores.unsqueeze(-1) * response_mask

    return scores, scores


@register_adv_est(AdvantageEstimator.GRPO_VECTORIZED)
def compute_grpo_vectorized_outcome_advantage(
    token_level_rewards: torch.Tensor,
    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
    index: np.ndarray,
    epsilon: float = 1e-6,
    norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo: bool = True,
    config: Optional[AlgoConfig] = None,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    Vectorized GRPO（outcome-only）:
      For each group g:
      a_i = \\frac{r_i - \\mu_g}{\\sigma_g} (or without dividing by \\sigma_g),
      then broadcast the scalar across the token dimension (multiplied by response_mask).。
    """
    with torch.no_grad():
        scores = token_level_rewards.sum(dim=-1)
        g = as_torch_index(index, device=scores.device)
        mean_g, std_g, _ = group_mean_std(scores, g, eps=0.0, device=scores.device)
        if norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo:
            scalars = (scores - mean_g[g]) / (std_g[g] + epsilon)
        else:
            scalars = scores - mean_g[g]
        advantages = scalars.unsqueeze(-1) * response_mask
        return advantages, advantages


@register_adv_est(AdvantageEstimator.GDPO)  # or simply: @register_adv_est("gdpo")
def compute_gdpo_outcome_advantage(
    token_level_rewards: torch.Tensor,
    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
    index: np.ndarray,
    epsilon: float = 1e-6,
    norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo: bool = True,
    config: Optional[AlgoConfig] = None,
    non_tensor_batch: Optional[dict] = None,
    batch: Optional[dict] = None,
    **kwargs,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    GDPO: Group reward-Decoupled Normalization Policy Optimization.

    Instead of summing all reward dimensions first (like GRPO), GDPO normalizes
    each reward dimension independently within each group before aggregation.
    This prevents a dominant reward signal from drowning out weaker ones.

    Mathematical formulation:
        Step 1 – Group-wise decoupled normalization (via GRPO per dimension):
            For each reward dimension k, within each group g:
            A_k = (r_k - μ_group(r_k)) / (σ_group(r_k) + ε)

        Step 2 – Weighted aggregation:
            A_sum = Σ_k w_k · A_k

        Step 3 – Batch-level normalization (via masked_whiten):
            A_final = whiten(A_sum, response_mask)

    Args:
        token_level_rewards: (bs, response_length) – standard token-level rewards.
            Used as fallback when per-dimension rewards are not provided.
        response_mask: (bs, response_length)
        index: (bs,) – group id per sample (from ``uid``).
        epsilon: Numerical stability constant.
        norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo: Whether to normalize by std in GRPO.
        config: Algorithm configuration (optional).
        non_tensor_batch: Non-tensor batch data containing per-dimension reward scores.
        batch: Batch data containing prompts, attention_mask, etc.

    Note:
        Ref GDPO (https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.05242).

    Returns:
        advantages: (bs, response_length)
        returns: (bs, response_length) – same as advantages (outcome-only).
    """
    score_list = None
    reward_weights = None

    if config is not None and non_tensor_batch is not None and batch is not None:
        gdpo_reward_keys = config.get("gdpo_reward_keys", None)
        assert gdpo_reward_keys, (
            "GDPO requires 'algorithm.gdpo_reward_keys' listing the individual reward "
            "component keys returned by compute_score (e.g. ['format_reward', 'accuracy_reward'])."
        )
        device = token_level_rewards.device
        prompt_length = batch["prompts"].size(1)
        valid_response_length = batch["attention_mask"][:, prompt_length:].sum(dim=1) - 1

        score_list = []
        for key in gdpo_reward_keys:
            assert key in non_tensor_batch, (
                f"GDPO reward key '{key}' not found in non_tensor_batch. "
                f"Available keys: {list(non_tensor_batch.keys())}. "
                f"Make sure your compute_score returns a dict containing '{key}'."
            )
            comp = non_tensor_batch[key]
            rm_score = torch.tensor(np.asarray(comp, dtype=np.float32), device=device)
            rm_scores = torch.zeros_like(response_mask, dtype=torch.float32)
            rm_scores[torch.arange(rm_scores.size(0), device=device), valid_response_length] = rm_score
            score_list.append(rm_scores)

        gdpo_weights = config.get("gdpo_reward_weights", None)
        if gdpo_weights is not None:
            reward_weights = list(gdpo_weights)

    if score_list is None:
        score_list = [token_level_rewards]

    num_scores = len(score_list)

    if reward_weights is not None:
        weights = torch.tensor(reward_weights, dtype=torch.float32, device=token_level_rewards.device)
    else:
        weights = torch.ones(num_scores, dtype=torch.float32, device=token_level_rewards.device)

    new_advantage = None

    for i in range(num_scores):
        normalized_score, _ = compute_grpo_outcome_advantage(
            token_level_rewards=score_list[i],
            response_mask=response_mask,
            index=index,
            epsilon=epsilon,
            norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo=norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo,
            config=config,
        )

        if new_advantage is None:
            new_advantage = weights[i] * normalized_score
        else:
            new_advantage += weights[i] * normalized_score

    advantages = verl_F.masked_whiten(new_advantage, response_mask) * response_mask

    return advantages, advantages


@register_adv_est(AdvantageEstimator.GRPO_PASSK)  # or simply: @register_adv_est("grpo_passk")
def compute_grpo_passk_outcome_advantage(
    token_level_rewards: torch.Tensor,
    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
    index: np.ndarray,
    epsilon: float = 1e-6,
    norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo: bool = True,
    config: Optional[AlgoConfig] = None,
    **kwargs,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    Compute advantage for Pass@k using a GRPO-style outcome reward formulation.
    Only the best response per group gets a non-zero advantage: r_max - r_second_max.

    Implemented as described in https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.19595.

    Args:
        token_level_rewards: (bs, response_length)
        response_mask: (bs, response_length)
        index: (bs,) → group ID per sample
        epsilon: float for numerical stability
        config: (AlgoConfig) algorithm settings, which contains "norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo"

    Returns:
        advantages: (bs, response_length)
        returns: (bs, response_length)
    """
    assert config is not None
    # if True, normalize advantage by std within group
    norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo = config.get("norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo", True)
    scores = token_level_rewards.sum(dim=-1)  # (bs,)
    advantages = torch.zeros_like(scores)

    id2scores = defaultdict(list)
    id2indices = defaultdict(list)

    with torch.no_grad():
        bsz = scores.shape[0]
        for i in range(bsz):
            idx = index[i]
            id2scores[idx].append(scores[i])
            id2indices[idx].append(i)

        for idx in id2scores:
            rewards = torch.stack(id2scores[idx])  # (k,)
            if rewards.numel() < 2:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Pass@k requires at least 2 samples per group. Got {rewards.numel()} for group {idx}."
                )
            topk, topk_idx = torch.topk(rewards, 2)
            r_max, r_second_max = topk[0], topk[1]
            i_max = id2indices[idx][topk_idx[0].item()]
            advantage = r_max - r_second_max
            if norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo:
                std = torch.std(rewards)
                advantage = advantage / (std + epsilon)
            advantages[i_max] = advantage

    advantages = advantages.unsqueeze(-1) * response_mask
    return advantages, advantages


@register_adv_est(
    AdvantageEstimator.REINFORCE_PLUS_PLUS_BASELINE
)  # or simply: @register_adv_est("reinforce_plus_plus_baseline")
def compute_reinforce_plus_plus_baseline_outcome_advantage(
    token_level_rewards: torch.Tensor,
    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
    index: torch.Tensor,
    epsilon: float = 1e-6,
    config: Optional[AlgoConfig] = None,
    **kwargs,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    Compute advantage for RF++-baseline (https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.03262), operating only on Outcome reward
    (with only one scalar reward for each response).

    Args:
        token_level_rewards: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
        response_mask: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
        config: (AlgoConfig) algorithm config

    Returns:
        advantages: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
        Returns: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
    """
    response_length = token_level_rewards.shape[-1]
    scores = token_level_rewards.sum(dim=-1)

    id2score = defaultdict(list)
    id2mean = {}

    with torch.no_grad():
        bsz = scores.shape[0]
        for i in range(bsz):
            id2score[index[i]].append(scores[i])
        for idx in id2score:
            if len(id2score[idx]) == 1:
                id2mean[idx] = torch.tensor(0.0)
            elif len(id2score[idx]) > 1:
                id2mean[idx] = torch.mean(torch.stack(id2score[idx]))
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"no score in prompt index: {idx}")
        for i in range(bsz):
            scores[i] = scores[i] - id2mean[index[i]]

        scores = scores.unsqueeze(-1).tile([1, response_length]) * response_mask
        scores = verl_F.masked_whiten(scores, response_mask) * response_mask

    return scores, scores


@register_adv_est(AdvantageEstimator.RLOO)  # or simply: @register_adv_est("rloo")
def compute_rloo_outcome_advantage(
    token_level_rewards: torch.Tensor,
    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
    index: np.ndarray,
    epsilon: float = 1e-6,
    config: Optional[AlgoConfig] = None,
    **kwargs,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    Compute advantage for RLOO based on https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14740

    Args:
        token_level_rewards: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
        response_mask: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
        config: (AlgoConfig) algorithm config

    Returns:
        advantages: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
        Returns: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
    """
    scores = token_level_rewards.sum(dim=-1)

    id2score = defaultdict(list)
    id2mean = {}

    with torch.no_grad():
        bsz = scores.shape[0]
        for i in range(bsz):
            id2score[index[i]].append(scores[i])
        for idx in id2score:
            if len(id2score[idx]) == 1:
                id2mean[idx] = torch.tensor(0.0)
            elif len(id2score[idx]) > 1:
                id2mean[idx] = torch.mean(torch.stack(id2score[idx]))
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"no score in prompt index: {idx}")
        for i in range(bsz):
            response_num = len(id2score[index[i]])
            if response_num > 1:
                scores[i] = scores[i] * response_num / (response_num - 1) - id2mean[index[i]] * response_num / (
                    response_num - 1
                )
        scores = scores.unsqueeze(-1) * response_mask

    return scores, scores


@register_adv_est(AdvantageEstimator.OPO)  # or simply: @register_adv_est("opo")
def compute_opo_outcome_advantage(
    token_level_rewards: torch.Tensor,
    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
    index: np.ndarray,
    epsilon: float = 1e-6,
    config: Optional[AlgoConfig] = None,
    **kwargs,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    Compute advantage for OPO based on https://arxiv.org/pdf/2505.23585

    Args:
        token_level_rewards: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
        response_mask: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
        config: (AlgoConfig) algorithm config

    Returns:
        advantages: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
        Returns: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
    """
    response_length = response_mask.sum(dim=-1)
    scores = token_level_rewards.sum(dim=-1)

    id2score = defaultdict(list)
    id2len = defaultdict(list)
    id2bsl = {}

    with torch.no_grad():
        bsz = scores.shape[0]
        for i in range(bsz):
            id2score[index[i]].append(scores[i])
            id2len[index[i]].append(response_length[i])

        for idx in id2score:
            if len(id2score[idx]) == 1:
                id2bsl[idx] = torch.tensor(0.0)
            elif len(id2score[idx]) > 1:
                score_tensor = torch.stack(id2score[idx])
                len_tensor = torch.stack(id2len[idx])
                id2bsl[idx] = (len_tensor * score_tensor).sum() / len_tensor.sum()
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"no score in prompt index: {idx}")
        for i in range(bsz):
            scores[i] = scores[i] - id2bsl[index[i]]
        scores = scores.unsqueeze(-1) * response_mask

    return scores, scores


@register_adv_est(AdvantageEstimator.REINFORCE_PLUS_PLUS)  # or simply: @register_adv_est("reinforce_plus_plus")
def compute_reinforce_plus_plus_outcome_advantage(
    token_level_rewards: torch.Tensor, response_mask: torch.Tensor, config: Optional[AlgoConfig] = None, **kwargs
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    Compute advantage for REINFORCE++.
    This implementation is based on the paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.03262

    Args:
        token_level_rewards: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
        response_mask: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
        config: (AlgoConfig) algorithm config

    Returns:
        advantages: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
        Returns: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
    """
    assert config is not None
    gamma = config.gamma
    with torch.no_grad():
        returns = torch.zeros_like(token_level_rewards)
        running_return = 0

        for t in reversed(range(token_level_rewards.shape[1])):
            running_return = token_level_rewards[:, t] + gamma * running_return
            returns[:, t] = running_return
            # Reset after EOS
            running_return = running_return * response_mask[:, t]

        advantages = verl_F.masked_whiten(returns, response_mask)
        advantages = advantages * response_mask

    return advantages, returns


@register_adv_est(AdvantageEstimator.REMAX)  # or simply: @register_adv_est("remax")
def compute_remax_outcome_advantage(
    token_level_rewards: torch.Tensor,
    reward_baselines: torch.Tensor,
    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
    config: Optional[AlgoConfig] = None,
    **kwargs,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    Compute advantage for ReMax, operating only on Outcome reward
    This implementation is based on the paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.10505
    (with only one scalar reward for each response).

    Args:
        token_level_rewards: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
        reward_baselines: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs,)
        response_mask: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
        config: (AlgoConfig) algorithm config

    Returns:
        advantages: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
        Returns: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
    """

    with torch.no_grad():
        returns = (token_level_rewards * response_mask).flip(dims=[-1]).cumsum(dim=-1).flip(dims=[-1])
        advantages = returns - reward_baselines.unsqueeze(-1) * response_mask

    return advantages, returns


@register_adv_est(AdvantageEstimator.GPG)  # or simply: @register_adv_est("gpg")
def compute_gpg_outcome_advantage(
    token_level_rewards: torch.Tensor,
    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
    index: np.ndarray,
    epsilon: float = 1e-6,
    f_norm: float = 1.0,
    alpha: float = 1.0,
    config=None,
    **kwargs,
):
    """
    Compute advantage for GPG, operating only on Outcome reward
    (with only one scalar reward for each response).
    Args:
        token_level_rewards: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
        response_mask: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
        index: `(np.ndarray)`
            shape: (bs,)
        epsilon: (float)
        f_norm: (float)
        alpha: (float)
        config: (dict) algorithm config

    Returns:
        advantages: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
        Returns: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
    """
    scores = token_level_rewards.sum(dim=-1)

    id2score = defaultdict(list)
    id2mean = {}
    id2std = {}

    with torch.no_grad():
        bsz = scores.shape[0]
        m = torch.count_nonzero(scores)
        alpha = bsz / m.clamp(min=1)

        for i in range(bsz):
            id2score[index[i]].append(scores[i])

        for idx in id2score:
            if len(id2score[idx]) == 1:
                id2mean[idx] = torch.tensor(0.0)
                id2std[idx] = torch.tensor(1.0)
            elif len(id2score[idx]) > 1:
                scores_tensor = torch.stack(id2score[idx])
                id2mean[idx] = torch.mean(scores_tensor)
                id2std[idx] = torch.std(scores_tensor)
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"no score in prompt index: {idx}")
        for i in range(bsz):
            scores[i] = alpha * (scores[i] - id2mean[index[i]]) / (f_norm)
        scores = scores.unsqueeze(-1) * response_mask

    return scores, scores


@register_adv_est(AdvantageEstimator.RLOO_VECTORIZED)  # or simply: @register_adv_est("rloo_vectorized")
def compute_rloo_vectorized_outcome_advantage(
    token_level_rewards: torch.Tensor,
    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
    index: np.ndarray,
    epsilon: float = 1e-6,
    config: Optional[AlgoConfig] = None,
    **kwargs,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    Compute advantage for RLOO based on https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14740

    Args:
        token_level_rewards: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
        response_mask: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
        config: (AlgoConfig) algorithm config

    Returns:
        advantages: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
        Returns: `(torch.Tensor)`
            shape: (bs, response_length)
    """
    scores = token_level_rewards.sum(dim=-1)

    with torch.no_grad():
        inv = torch.from_numpy(np.unique(index, return_inverse=True)[1]).to(scores.device)

        c = torch.bincount(inv)[inv].to(scores.dtype)
        adv = ((c * scores - torch.bincount(inv, weights=scores)[inv]) / (c - 1).clamp_min(1)) * (c > 1)

        adv = adv.unsqueeze(-1) * response_mask

    return adv, adv


@register_adv_est(AdvantageEstimator.OPTIMAL_TOKEN_BASELINE)
def compute_optimal_token_baseline_advantage(
    token_level_rewards: torch.Tensor,
    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
    index: np.ndarray,
    old_log_probs: torch.Tensor,
    sum_pi_squared: torch.Tensor,
    rollout_is_weights: torch.Tensor = None,
    handle_zero_tail: bool = True,
    epsilon: float = 1e-8,
    **kwargs,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    Compute advantages using Optimal Token Baseline (OTB).

    Unlike the group mean based baseline which uses a single baseline per trajectory,
    this computes a unique baseline for each timestep using cumulative path variance.

    Theory:
        For each timestep t in each prompt group:
            B_t* = E[G_t × W_t] / E[W_t]
        where W_t = Σ_{j=1}^t ||s_j||² (cumulative path-variance proxy)
        and ||s_j||² = 1 - 2π_j + Σπ²

    The cumulative sum W_t captures the "realized energy" of trajectory has been up to timestep t,
    giving higher weight to predicting rewards on high-variance paths.

    Args:
        token_level_rewards: Rewards at each token position [shape: (bs, response_length)]
        response_mask: Binary mask for valid tokens (1) vs padding (0) [shape: (bs, response_length)]
        index: Prompt indices for grouping trajectories from same prompt [shape: (bs,)]
        old_log_probs: Log probabilities from training policy during generation [shape: (bs, response_length)]
        sum_pi_squared: Sum of squared probabilities over vocabulary Σπ² [shape: (bs, response_length)]
        rollout_is_weights: Pre-computed IS weights for W correction [shape: (bs, response_length)],
            None if not using IS
        handle_zero_tail: If True, zero baselines will be set in the portion of the longest trajectory
            that extends beyond the second-longest trajectory in the prompt group.
            Default: True
        epsilon: Small constant for numerical stability (default: 1e-8)

    Returns:
        advantages: OTB advantage estimates [shape: (bs, response_length)]
        returns: Cumulative rewards (returns) from each position [shape: (bs, response_length)]

    Note on Rollout Importance Sampling:
        When rollout_is_weights is provided, W_t is scaled by ρ̄²(t) to minimize MSE under truncated IS:
            B_t* = Σ[G_t × ρ̄²(t) × W_t] / Σ[ρ̄²(t) × W_t]
    """
    with torch.no_grad():
        batch_size, seq_len = token_level_rewards.shape
        device = token_level_rewards.device

        # Compute returns (reward-to-go) for each timestep
        returns = (token_level_rewards * response_mask).flip(dims=[-1]).cumsum(dim=-1).flip(dims=[-1])

        # Step 1: Compute w_per_timestep = 1 - 2π_t + Σπ²)
        pi_t = torch.exp(old_log_probs)
        w_per_timestep = 1 - 2 * pi_t + sum_pi_squared

        # Step 2: Apply rollout importance sampling correction (if enabled)
        if rollout_is_weights is not None:
            # Scale W by ρ̄² to minimize MSE under truncated IS
            w_per_timestep = w_per_timestep * (rollout_is_weights**2)

        # Step 3: Compute cumulative path-variance proxy: W_t = Σ_{j=1}^t w_j
        # This measures accumulated variance from the start of the trajectory up to timestep t
        w_cumulative = (w_per_timestep * response_mask).cumsum(dim=-1)

        # Group trajectories by prompt
        prompt_groups = defaultdict(list)
        for i in range(batch_size):
            prompt_groups[index[i]].append(i)

        # Initialize baselines tensor [batch_size, seq_len]
        baselines = torch.zeros_like(returns)

        # Compute per-step baseline for each prompt group
        for _, trajectory_indices in prompt_groups.items():
            N = len(trajectory_indices)
            if N == 1:
                # Single trajectory - no baseline (advantage = return)
                continue

            traj_idx = torch.tensor(trajectory_indices, device=device)

            # Extract group data [N, seq_len]
            returns_group = returns[traj_idx]
            w_cumulative_group = w_cumulative[traj_idx]
            mask_group = response_mask[traj_idx]

            # Compute per-timestep baseline: B_t = Σ[G_t × W_t] / Σ[W_t]
            # where W_t = Σ_{j=1}^t ||s_j||² (cumulative path variance)
            # Shape: [seq_len]
            numerator = (returns_group * w_cumulative_group * mask_group).sum(dim=0)  # Sum over trajectories
            denominator = (w_cumulative_group * mask_group).sum(dim=0) + epsilon

            baseline_per_step = numerator / denominator  # [seq_len]

            # Assign to all trajectories in this group
            baselines[traj_idx] = baseline_per_step.unsqueeze(0).expand(N, -1)

            if handle_zero_tail:
                # Optionally zero out the portion of the longest trajectory that extends
                # beyond the second-longest trajectory in the prompt group.
                response_lengths = mask_group.sum(dim=-1)
                sorted_lengths, _ = torch.sort(response_lengths)
                max_length = int(sorted_lengths[-1].item())
                second_max_length = int(sorted_lengths[-2].item())
                max_length_idx = (response_lengths == max_length).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
                if max_length_idx.numel() == 1 and max_length > second_max_length:
                    max_length_traj_idx = trajectory_indices[int(max_length_idx[0])]
                    baselines[max_length_traj_idx, second_max_length:] = 0.0

        # Compute advantages: A_t = G_t - B_t
        advantages = (returns - baselines) * response_mask

    return advantages, returns


@register_adv_est(AdvantageEstimator.TIR_OPTIMAL_TOKEN_BASELINE)
def compute_multi_turn_optimal_token_baseline_advantage(
    token_level_rewards: torch.Tensor,
    response_mask: torch.Tensor,
    index: np.ndarray,
    old_log_probs: torch.Tensor,
    sum_pi_squared: torch.Tensor,
    rollout_is_weights: torch.Tensor = None,
    handle_zero_tail: bool = True,
    epsilon: float = 1e-8,
    **kwargs,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    Compute advantages using Optimal Token Baseline (OTB).

    Unlike the group mean based baseline which uses a single baseline per trajectory,
    this computes a unique baseline for each timestep using cumulative path variance.

    Theory:
        For each timestep t in each prompt group:
            B_t* = E[G_t × W_t] / E[W_t]
        where W_t = Σ_{j=1}^t ||s_j||² (cumulative path-variance proxy)
        and ||s_j||² = 1 - 2π_j + Σπ²

    The cumulative sum W_t captures the "realized energy" of trajectory has been up to timestep t,
    giving higher weight to predicting rewards on high-variance paths.

    Args:
        token_level_rewards: Rewards at each token position [shape: (bs, response_length)]
        response_mask: Binary mask for valid tokens (1) vs padding (0) [shape: (bs, response_length)]
        index: Prompt indices for grouping trajectories from same prompt [shape: (bs,)]
        old_log_probs: Log probabilities from training policy during generation [shape: (bs, response_length)]
        sum_pi_squared: Sum of squared probabilities over vocabulary Σπ² [shape: (bs, response_length)]
        rollout_is_weights: Pre-computed IS weights for W correction [shape: (bs, response_length)],
            None if not using IS
        handle_zero_tail: If True, zero baselines will be set in the portion of the longest trajectory
            that extends beyond the second-longest trajectory in the prompt group.
            Default: False
        epsilon: Small constant for numerical stability (default: 1e-8)

    Returns:
        advantages: OTB advantage estimates [shape: (bs, response_length)]
        returns: Cumulative rewards (returns) from each position [shape: (bs, response_length)]

    Note on Rollout Importance Sampling:
        When rollout_is_weights is provided, W_t is scaled by ρ̄²(t) to minimize MSE under truncated IS:
            B_t* = Σ[G_t × ρ̄²(t) × W_t] / Σ[ρ̄²(t) × W_t]
    """
    with torch.no_grad():
        # Compute returns (reward-to-go) for each timestep
        token_returns = (token_level_rewards * response_mask).flip(dims=[-1]).cumsum(dim=-1).flip(dims=[-1])

        # Step 1: Compute w_per_timestep = 1 - 2π_t + Σπ²)
        pi_t = torch.exp(old_log_probs)
        w_per_timestep = 1 - 2 * pi_t + sum_pi_squared

        # Step 2: Apply rollout importance sampling correction (if enabled)
        if rollout_is_weights is not None:
            # Scale W by ρ̄² to minimize MSE under truncated IS
            w_per_timestep = w_per_timestep * (rollout_is_weights**2)

        # Step 3: Compute cumulative path-variance proxy: W_t = Σ_{j=1}^t w_j
        # This measures accumulated variance from the start of the trajectory up to timestep t
        w_cumulative = (w_per_timestep * response_mask).cumsum(dim=-1)

        # Step 4: Concatenate returns and w_cumulative for each trajectory
        # This allows us to compute baseline per timestep for each trajectory
        response_lengths = response_mask.sum(dim=-1).to(dtype=torch.long)  # [shape: (bs * n, )]
        max_response_length = int(response_lengths.max().item()) if response_lengths.numel() > 0 else 0
        all_w_values = w_cumulative.new_zeros(
            (len(response_lengths), max_response_length)
        )  # [shape: (bs * n, max_response_length)]
        all_returns = torch.zeros_like(all_w_values)
        for i in range(len(response_lengths)):
            length = int(response_lengths[i].item())
            if length == 0:
                continue
            mask = response_mask[i].bool()
            all_w_values[i, :length] = w_cumulative[i, mask]
            all_returns[i, :length] = token_returns[i, mask]

        # Group trajectories by prompt
        prompt_groups = defaultdict(list)
        for i in range(len(response_lengths)):
            if response_lengths[i] == 0:
                continue
            prompt_groups[index[i]].append(i)

        # Compute optimal baseline for each prompt group
        baselines = torch.zeros_like(all_returns)

        for _, trajectory_indices in prompt_groups.items():
            N = len(trajectory_indices)
            traj_idx = torch.tensor(trajectory_indices, device=all_returns.device)

            if N == 1:
                # Single trajectory - no baseline (keep original reward as advantage)
                baselines[traj_idx[0]] = 0.0
                continue

            # Extract group data
            w_group = all_w_values[traj_idx]  # [shape: (N, max_response_length)]
            R_group = all_returns[traj_idx]  # [shape: (N, max_response_length)]
            # Direct optimal baseline - single value for all in group
            b_star = (R_group * w_group).sum(dim=0) / (w_group.sum(dim=0) + epsilon)
            # Convert to match baselines dtype (epsilon can cause float64 promotion)
            baselines[traj_idx] = b_star.to(baselines.dtype)

            if handle_zero_tail:
                # Optionally zero out the portion of the longest trajectory that extends
                # beyond the second-longest trajectory in the prompt group.
                response_lengths_group = response_lengths[traj_idx]
                sorted_lengths, _ = torch.sort(response_lengths_group)
                max_length = int(sorted_lengths[-1].item())
                second_max_length = int(sorted_lengths[-2].item())
                max_length_idx = (response_lengths_group == max_length).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
                if max_length_idx.numel() == 1 and max_length > second_max_length:
                    max_length_traj_idx = trajectory_indices[int(max_length_idx[0])]
                    baselines[max_length_traj_idx, second_max_length:] = 0.0

        # Compute advantages
        all_advantages = all_returns - baselines  # [shape: (bs * n, max_response_length)]

        advantages = torch.zeros_like(token_returns)  # [shape: (bs * n, turn * response_length)]
        for i in range(len(response_lengths)):
            if response_lengths[i] == 0:
                continue
            advantages[i, response_mask[i].bool()] = all_advantages[i, : response_lengths[i]]

        advantages = advantages * response_mask  # [shape: (bs * n * turn, response_length)]

    return advantages, token_returns


def compute_rewards(token_level_scores, old_log_prob, ref_log_prob, kl_ratio):
    """Compute token-level rewards with KL penalty.

    Args:
        token_level_scores (torch.Tensor): Token-level reward scores.
        old_log_prob (torch.Tensor): Log probabilities from current policy.
        ref_log_prob (torch.Tensor): Log probabilities from reference policy.
        kl_ratio (float): KL penalty coefficient.

    Returns:
        torch.Tensor: Token-level rewards with KL penalty applied.
    """
    kl = old_log_prob - ref_log_prob
    return token_level_scores - kl * kl_ratio


def agg_loss(
    loss_mat: torch.Tensor,
    loss_mask: torch.Tensor,
    loss_agg_mode: str,
    dp_size: int = 1,
    batch_num_tokens: Optional[int] = None,
    global_batch_size: Optional[int] = None,
    loss_scale_factor: Optional[int] = None,
):
    """
